headline: NATO's top commander in Europe is drafting a plan to defeat a Russian attack on the alliance's eastern flank using drones, AI and regular forces.
score_reason: Kept at the pool score: a major allied defence plan, but only a draft not yet presented, and NATO gave no details.
importance_line: People living along NATO's eastern flank and the allied governments urged to spend more, and to choose between tanks and newer drone and AI systems, are most affected, but the plan is a draft not yet presented, partly rests on unnamed officials, and NATO declined to discuss its details.
summary: Bloomberg reports that US General Alexus Grynkewich, NATO's top commander in Europe, is preparing a "theory of victory" under which NATO would meet a Russian attack on its eastern flank by blocking it with land forces plus low-cost drones, machines with minimal crews and AI-enabled targeting, then destroying Russian command and control to win quickly. Bloomberg has seen an unclassified version, which Grynkewich is due to present in Poland on 12 Oct 2026; his spokesman declined to give details and called the alliance "purely defensive", and Secretary-General Mark Rutte has said there are no signs Russia is preparing a conventional attack.
